articles.headline: Senate concludes plenary debate on proposed ₱7.2 trillion 2027 budget
articles.descriptionHtml: The Senate wrapped marathon plenary deliberations on the proposed ₱7.2-trillion 2027 national budget early November 28, after the chamber suspended Sara Duterte’s impeachment trial to clear the calendar. Senators also realigned ₱19.8 billion from medical-assistance and crisis-aid lines to boost PhilHealth’s subsidy, approved the Office of the Vice President’s budget in about a minute on November 26, and passed the Office of the President’s budget in roughly two minutes on November 24. The measure still faces bicameral amendments before final enactment.
articles.diasporaImpact: Health subsidies and agency spending in the 2027 budget shape services and benefits many families at home rely on.

articles.headline: Impeachment court subpoenas Cale88 co-owner and customs official
articles.descriptionHtml: On November 26 the Senate impeachment court confirmed subpoenas for Dr. Lourdes Tingson-Lebosada, a co-owner of Cale88 Foods Corporation, and Bureau of Customs deputy commissioner Agaton Teodoro Uvero to testify when Sara Duterte’s trial resumes December 1–4. The defense seeks testimony on Cale88’s ownership, finances, and export records amid allegations of unexplained wealth. The court finished serving both witnesses ahead of the December hearings.
articles.diasporaImpact: The trial tests national institutions and may shape political confidence among Filipinos abroad.

articles.headline: Sandiganbayan denies Marcoleta's bail in ₱75 million plunder case
articles.descriptionHtml: The Sandiganbayan Third Division denied bail on November 23 to Senator Rodante Marcoleta and three co-accused in a ₱75-million plunder case over campaign donations prosecutors say he failed to declare. Justices ruled the evidence of guilt was strong, citing donor’s-tax payments that undercut his claim the transfers were exempt electoral contributions. Marcoleta, former representative Mike Defensor, and two businessmen remain detained in Payatas jail; Marcoleta has been suspended from the Senate since October.
articles.diasporaImpact: Corruption cases against sitting lawmakers signal how accountability rules are applied at the top of Philippine politics.

articles.headline: Supreme Court dismisses Duterte arrest petitions as Hague trial looms
articles.descriptionHtml: On November 24 the Supreme Court dismissed habeas corpus petitions challenging Rodrigo Duterte’s March 2025 arrest, saying Philippine courts cannot direct his detention at the ICC in The Hague. The ICC confirmed on November 27 that his trial opens November 30. On November 23 the Truth Commission reported an initial registry of 8,320 drug-war killings and said the campaign appeared state-organized; the justice secretary said the Department of Justice would review the findings.
articles.diasporaImpact: Accountability for the drug war and ICC proceedings are closely watched by families who lost relatives or fear renewed violence.

articles.headline: Manila says no agreed terms on Trump's US-only import claim
articles.descriptionHtml: After Donald Trump said on November 22 that the Philippines would buy all agricultural and energy imports from the United States by January 1, Malacañang said November 24 that President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. had not agreed to terms or a timeline. Cabinet officials said negotiations continue, private firms choose suppliers, and Manila would keep multiple sources if US prices are not competitive. The gap between Trump’s claim and Philippine statements leaves trade obligations unsettled.
articles.diasporaImpact: Unsettled trade terms could eventually affect food and fuel prices for households, but no binding deal is in place yet.

articles.headline: Philippines warns against recruitment scams sending workers to war zones
articles.descriptionHtml: On November 28 the Department of National Defense and Department of Migrant Workers warned Filipinos against illegal recruitment that routes job seekers toward conflict areas. During Senate budget debates lawmakers cited a viral appeal from about 30 workers allegedly duped into bunker construction in Russian-occupied Ukraine after being hired for janitorial or construction jobs. The DMW said it is coordinating with foreign affairs, defense, and law-enforcement agencies to locate them.
articles.diasporaImpact: Overseas Filipinos and their families should verify recruiters and job orders before accepting high-risk offers abroad.

articles.headline: Nine provinces in drought as El Niño spread forecast widens
articles.descriptionHtml: PAGASA said on November 26 that nine provinces were already in meteorological drought, with 29 more in dry spell. Its November climate forum projected drought in 29 provinces by end-December, 47 by end-January, and 68 by end-February as rainfall stays below normal. The United States pledged $4 million through the World Food Programme to aid about 38,000 vulnerable families in Eastern Visayas and Bicol; state climatologists expect El Niño impacts to persist into 2027.
articles.diasporaImpact: Families abroad may need to track water, power, and farm advisories as drought expands across more provinces.
